grammar.label: summarising a long argument without falsifying it
grammar.form: the proportional summary; keeping the hedges; naming what was cut
grammar.meaning: compresses a text while preserving its claims and their strength

explanation.en: Most summaries fail by promoting: a hedged claim becomes a flat one because the hedge took words and the claim did not. A summary that says 'she argues, tentatively' in four words has preserved something the shorter version destroyed. Where you cut, say so.
explanation.uz: Ko'p xulosalar da'voni kuchaytirib yuborish bilan xato qiladi: ehtiyotkor da'vo tekis da'voga aylanadi, chunki ehtiyotkorlik so'z talab qiladi.

grammar.positive_example: She argues, tentatively, that the two are connected; I have not summarised her method.
grammar.negative_example: She shows that the two are connected.

l1_notes.uz: Xulosalashda ehtiyotkor iboralarni saqlash — ingliz ilmiy odobining bir qismi.

grammar.label: the accurate quotation and the ellipsis that distorts
grammar.form: square brackets for changes; ellipsis for cuts; [sic]; the rule against cutting a qualification
grammar.meaning: reproduces someone's words without changing what they said

explanation.en: Cutting 'in most cases' out of a quotation with an ellipsis is technically marked and substantively dishonest. The conventions — brackets, ellipsis, [sic] — exist to make every change visible, and they are easy to satisfy while still misrepresenting. The real rule is that the quotation must mean what the speaker meant.
explanation.uz: Iqtibosdan 'ko'p hollarda' iborasini olib tashlash texnik jihatdan belgilangan, mazmunan esa halol emas. Qoidalar o'zgarishni ko'rsatish uchun; ularni bajarib ham chalg'itish mumkin.

grammar.positive_example: She said it held 'in most cases', and I have kept those three words.
grammar.negative_example: She said the rule held '… without exception in the recorded period'.

l1_notes.uz: Iqtibos qoidalari texnik, lekin ularga rioya qilib ham ma'noni buzish mumkin.

body.text: Your summary of her chapter is three lines and all three are about the last page.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is the part I disagreed with.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: So your reader learns what you object to and never learns what she said. A summary keeps her proportions, not yours.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Six lines on the argument and one on the objection.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And the objection clearly marked as yours. Now the quotation on page two.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The evidence shows that the policy worked.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Read me the whole sentence out of her book.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The evidence, if the two smallest districts are set aside, shows that the policy worked.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: You cut the middle out and the meaning changed. That is not making it shorter. That is rewriting her.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The three dots tell the reader that something was removed. They do not tell her it was the condition the entire claim depends on.
